newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates close down as squeeze eases.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates close down as squeeze eases.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates finished sharply lower on Friday, with payments returning to the banking system replenishing liquidity despite a continuing exodus of funds into the red-hot stock market, dealers said.

The overnight interbank rate eased to end at 7.466 percent against Thursday's 7.720 close -- well outside the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone but still below the record double-digit closes of late June.
The 30-day commercial paper eased to 7.25 percent against 7.50.
The stock market, furthering a long-running bull charge on huge turnover, closed 1.10 percent higher on Friday at 9,677.40, the index's highest level since April 27, 1990.
Turnover was voluminous at T$218 billion, though still far below Thursday's record T$297 billion.
The central bank continued its mop-up measures on Friday, issuing T$3 billion in two-month negotiable certificates of deposit at an average yield of 7.124 percent.
Dealers said despite the central bank's move, the money market drew enough liquidity from returning payments to enable rates to stabilise.
They expected the money rates to drift lower next week as many banks have reduced interest rates.
Government bond yields were locked into a narrow-range consolidation with investors stepping to the sidelines in the face of the stock bull run.
